AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: There have been few prospective studies on the association between anxiety disorders and adolescent obesity; none examine potential reciprocal effects.

AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this paper is to examine the prospective association between anxiety disorders and obesity among adolescents.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Using data from a two-wave, prospective study of 3134 adolescents, we examined reciprocal effects between body weight and DSM-IV anxiety disorders.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Weight status did not increase future risk of anxiety disorders nor did anxiety disorders at baseline increase risk of future obesity in the overall sample. Stratifying by gender revealed an increased risk of overweight and obesity in males with anxiety disorders, but not for females. Major depression did not mediate these associations.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Similar to prospective studies of depression, it appears anxiety disorders may increase risk of obesity. However, more research is needed on the role of psychopathology in adolescent obesity, in particular anxiety disorders and possible moderators (such as gender) and mediators.
